incident-bot: :rotating_light: DETECTED: api-gateway (edge-eu-west-1) elevated 502/504s. 5m window 5xx rate: 12.4% | affected endpoints: /v1/chat, /v1/generate. Notifying on-call.
Alex: I'm looking. Any recent rollouts? :mag_right:
deploy-bot: gateway-frontends rollout (canary) completed @1802590000. No active rollouts since then.
Sam: oncall here. Grafana shows spike starting ~08:12 UTC. Upstream health checks for model-router are green but connection-level errors at the edge are up.
Rob: pulling edge logs now. lots of `upstream_timed_out` entries. snippet:
```
2026-03-14T08:14:39Z edge-07 nginx: [warn] 504 while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.1.3.21, upstream: "http://10.0.11.8:8080/v1/chat"
```
Priya: k8s shows model-router pods stable. No restarts. CPU spiking on router workers though.
Carlos: traffic check: one API key (acct-qrs) accounts for a huge chunk of requests — mostly long-running streaming calls. Their concurrency spiked to ~450 concurrent connections.
Maya: CS reports multiple customers experiencing failures, one customer escalated. I've drafted a brief status update.
Jen: can we confirm whether these are timeouts while connecting (connect_timeout) or while waiting for response (read_timeout)? Rob?
Rob: majority are read timeouts. Upstream accepted connection but took too long to respond; nginx gave 504.
Alex: initial mitigation plan: 1) apply token-based throttling for acct-qrs 2) scale frontend pool quickly 3) reduce model-router max concurrency per worker to shed long-tail requests 4) temporarily increase proxy_read_timeout from 30s->90s. Which order?
Sam: scale frontends + rate-limit token first. Priya, can you push a rate-limit rule keyed to that API key and scale deployment?
Priya: applying rate-limit now. patching configmap and restarting frontends.
(30s)
Priya: rate-limit rule active: acct-qrs -> 120r/s. frontends scaled from 5->15. Monitoring.
Sam: some improvement in error rate but still intermittent 504s on heavy requests.
Carlos: acct-qrs traffic pattern shows many long sequence generations (avg token count high). They open connections for long-running streams which tie up worker slots.
Alex: let's reduce model-router concurrency per process to 10 from 32 to force backpressure upstream and drop some concurrency at the edge.
Priya: updating model-router env MAX_CONCURRENCY=10 and restarting.
(deploy-bot): rollout/model-router v2.3.8 -> updating pods
Priya: model-router pods coming up healthy.
Sam: after reducing concurrency and rate-limiting, 5xx down from 12% -> 3.7%. But p95 still elevated.
Rob: still observe `upstream response timeout` for a subset of requests with very long runtimes. Given lower concurrency, we can temporarily increase proxy_read_timeout to avoid spuriously cutting long valid requests.
Alex: increase to 120s for now, but plan to revert. Rob, patch nginx configmap and restart edge.
Rob: applying change:
```
kubectl -n infra patch configmap nginx-edge-config --patch '{"data":{"proxy_read_timeout":"120s"}}'
kubectl rollout restart daemonset/nginx-edge
```
Rob: done. watching.
(2 minutes)
Sam: errors falling further. 5xx at ~0.9%, p95 latency 780ms. Still a few 504s tied to a particular request pattern.
Maya: updating status: "Experiencing elevated 502/504s due to traffic spike from single customer. Mitigations in progress: throttling, scaling, router config changes. Monitoring."
Maya: posted to status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-20260314-02
Carlos: proposing a circuit-breaker rule: if a token has >200 concurrent streams in a 60s window, return 429. I'll prepare the rule.
Sam: apply the circuit-breaker.
Carlos: circuit-breaker applied. patch:
```
kubectl -n infra apply -f cb-acct-qrs.yaml
```
(3 minutes)
Sam: traffic returning to baseline. 5xx now 0.4%, p95 310ms, no 504s in last 4 minutes.
Alex: solid. Keep elevated timeouts and reduced concurrency for 30m, then revert if stable. Priya, schedule an automated check and revert jobs.
Priya: scheduled: in 30m, if 5xx < 0.5% for 20m, revert MAX_CONCURRENCY to 32 and proxy_read_timeout to 30s.
Rob: pulled traces for sample 0f9e8d7c, saved to s3://redwood-logs/incidents/1802604321/trace-0f9e8d7c.json
Jen: severity: keeping at P2 until we see sustained stability. Will reassess.
Maya: customers notified. CS follow-ups assigned.
Alex: handoff: I'm offline in 18m. Sam take watch and handle the revert if safe.
Sam: taking handoff. I'll run 30m watch.
Priya: quick follow-ups added to runbook: (1) implement per-token concurrency caps upstream (2) autoscale model-router by active long-running streams, (3) prompt length heuristics to detect long-running sequences.
Rob: postmortem: I'll own logs and error classification. Priya: mitigation/action items owner.
incident-bot: Incident MITIGATED at 1802606789. Summary: Edge 502/504 spike caused by high-concurrency long-running streaming requests from single API key. Actions: rate-limited token, scaled frontends, reduced router concurrency, increased edge timeout, applied circuit-breaker. Postmortem owners: Rob + Priya. Link: https://internal.redwood.ai/postmortems/INC-20260314-02
Alex: great job. Keeping thread open for postmortem notes."
